title: Japan’s New CIA Could Be Takaichi’s Trump Card
gist: Excerpt of Derek Grossman's Foreign Policy piece: Japan under PM Takaichi is pursuing its biggest intelligence overhaul since 1945 to build a CIA-like foreign HUMINT agency by 2028, framed as a burden-sharing deliverable for Trump.

insights.claim: Japan aims to create its own version of the CIA by 2028 in the most substantial intelligence overhaul since 1945.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.quote: the most substantial overhaul of Japan’s intelligence collection and analysis capabilities since 1945
insights.locator: When Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi

insights.claim: The new agency is intended to run clandestine HUMINT abroad against China, North Korea and Russia, filling a gap left by postwar reticence rooted in imperial-era abuses.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Raises Japan's role in regional intelligence and deterrence.
insights.locator: Although its final name and structure

insights.claim: Intelligence reform is a less-noticed but consequential way Tokyo is assuming more responsibility for its own security, supporting Takaichi's pitch to Trump.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.quote: Intelligence reform may generate fewer headlines than higher defense spending
